title: Migration UX decision record

decisions.summary: Detect legacy session via inert signals (IndexedDB store names, credential envelope, fallback session keys, cutover marker) without starting matrix-js-sdk or opening crypto APIs.
Reauthentication is required for users with a legacy Matrix session at cutover; silent continuation on the old access token is not product policy.
Create a new Matrix device via normal login/SSO with platform display name Synara macOS or Synara Linux; do not claim the legacy device ID.
Do not copy access token, refresh token, or device ID from legacy JS session material into a fresh Rust crypto/state store by default (plan §8.1).
After reauth and Rust store open: guided recovery key / secret storage / key backup restore; deferral allowed only with explicit acknowledgement that encrypted history may be incomplete.
Mark complete only when Rust stores open, session secrets are native-persisted, sync readiness is confirmed, cutover marker is written, and no JS Matrix client was started.
Retain legacy Matrix IndexedDB inertly for a bounded window; never reopen it with matrix-js-sdk in the new product.
Explicit, idempotent, scoped cleanup of legacy Matrix IndexedDB names and legacy token keys only after successful transition; strong confirm for early cleanup; never drafts/settings/downloads.
Rollback means prior product build plus preserved inert legacy data within the retention window; not dual-runtime or in-app SDK selector.
Drafts, platform settings, downloads, and unrelated local configuration survive cutover, failure, and Matrix-scoped cleanup.
Separate store directories, keys, and session generations per account; sequential single-active isolation only—do not promise concurrent multi-account (FR-7.9-011 remains partial).
Logout and local wipe are distinct actions with distinct confirmations; crash recovery must not auto-wipe.
Honest one-time sign-in and recovery messaging; no secrets in copy; no dual-backend language; set expectations for encrypted history dependency on recovery.
Failed or crashed transition preserves legacy data, isolates incomplete Rust store generations, and always offers retry.
Hard constraint: no dual production backend, SDK selector, simultaneous JS+Rust clients, or permanent matrix-js-sdk runtime path after cutover.

happy_path_steps: Launch with Rust-only Matrix bootstrap (no matrix-js-sdk).
Detect legacy session using inert signals only.
Show one-time migration explanation (reauth + recovery expectations; drafts/settings kept).
Create new named device (Synara macOS / Synara Linux); no token/device import.
Open native Rust SQLite stores; bind store keys in OS credential store.
Persist new session envelope to native credential store after success path.
Guide key recovery / backup restore; allow explicit deferral with warning.
Start sync and wait for product readiness.
Write non-secret cutover completion marker; leave legacy IndexedDB inert.
Enter normal product shell with single Matrix owner.
Later offer scoped cleanup after retention window or early confirm.

open_parameters.notes: Requires strong confirmation that rollback via legacy data will no longer be possible.
Complete allowed with explicit deferral acknowledgement; must not claim E2EE history ready without recovery.

user_copy_principles: No secrets in copy, logs, or templates (tokens, recovery keys, passwords, device IDs, event plaintext).
Set expectations: one-time sign-in required; encrypted history depends on recovery key/backup.
Do not claim silent seamless migration.
State that drafts and settings are preserved.
State that older Matrix data remains unused until cleanup.
Honest failure: previous data not removed; retry available.
No dual-backend or 'use old engine' product language.
Prefer user-facing terms over internal SDK names in primary UI.

draft_user_copy.migration.title: Update your signed-in session
draft_user_copy.migration.body: Synara now uses a more secure session engine. You’ll sign in once more. Your drafts and settings stay on this computer. Encrypted message history is restored with your recovery key.
draft_user_copy.migration.learn_body: We don’t reuse your previous secure store automatically. After you sign in, we’ll help restore encryption keys if you have a recovery key. Older Matrix data on this device stays unused until you clean it up.
draft_user_copy.recovery.title: Restore encryption
draft_user_copy.recovery.body: Enter your recovery key to unlock encrypted message history on this device. We never send your recovery key to Synara servers as app telemetry.
draft_user_copy.recovery.defer_warn: Some older encrypted messages may not be readable until you restore.
draft_user_copy.transition.success: You’re set. Synara is ready on this device.
draft_user_copy.transition.failure: We couldn’t finish the update. Your previous data on this device was not removed. You can try again.
draft_user_copy.cleanup.title: Remove older Matrix data?
draft_user_copy.cleanup.body: This deletes unused data from the previous session engine on this device. Drafts and settings are kept. You can’t use that older data to roll back afterward.
draft_user_copy.logout.title: Sign out?
draft_user_copy.wipe.title: Delete local Matrix data?
draft_user_copy.wipe.body: This removes Synara’s Matrix data for this account on this device. It is different from signing out on the server.

failure_modes.user_outcome: Unsupported/migration state; do not complete with permanent WebView tokens
Do not mark complete; reconnect/retry guidance
Relaunch resumes incomplete migration; no auto-wipe

related_fr_notes.FR-7.9-001: implemented — store-before-sync boot order meaning retained under native SQLite cutover
related_fr_notes.FR-7.9-006: implemented — recovery product meaning rehomed to P8.5/P3.8
related_fr_notes.FR-7.9-011: partial — sequential single-active only; do not re-promote
related_fr_notes.FR-7.9-012: implemented — restore must not wipe healthy stores; identity change explicit
related_fr_notes.FR-7.9-013: partial — non-destructive anomaly guidance; no invented silent auto-wipe

phase0_note: Migration UX policy is decided for Phase 0 acceptance before session code is written. Implementation starts at Phase 3 (P3.7 and related auth tasks).
